title: Request routing fallback matrix — architecture scrub
content:
Meeting: Architecture scrub — request routing fallback matrix
Date: 2026-03-10 10:00-11:00 PT
Location: Zoom + notes doc
Attendees: Dana Kapoor (owner), Alex Li, Maya Jensen, Omar Rahman, Priya Menon, Samir Bose (SRE), Lina Torres (Product)
Purpose: Align on a compact, testable matrix that maps detection signals and failure modes to deterministic fallback actions (model variant, region, capacity tier, degradation policy). Surface tradeoffs for SLOs and rollout plan.

Agenda:
- Quick recap of existing fallback code paths (Alex)
- Failure signal taxonomy we observed in prod + incidents (Samir)
- Matrix proposal and examples (Dana)
- Alternatives considered and tradeoffs (group)
- Tests & rollout plan (Maya)
- Action items and owners

Notes / discussion highlights:
1) Failure signal taxonomy (from incident logs):
   - Hard failure: executor crash / OOM on GPU during token generation
   - Latency spike: 95th/99th latency breach for a given model instance pool
   - Capacity rejection: pool is at max concurrent requests and queue time > threshold
   - Soft quality regression: downstream evals show perplexity or hallucination metrics degrade beyond tolerance
   - Regional outage: cloud region incidents / networking latency to private deployments

2) Matrix proposal (summary):
   - Hard failure -> immediate switch to configured fallback model variant in same region (quantized / smaller architecture) + mark node unhealthy for fast reprovision; escalate to Dedicated fallback if tenant uses reserved capacity.
   - Latency spike -> short-circuit routing to lower-latency variant in same hw tier (e.g., smaller sequence length cap) and enable prefix-KV cache hit-only path; continue sampling a small % of traffic to original variant for monitoring.
   - Capacity rejection -> burst to cross-region standby pool if tenant policy allows cross-region fallback; else to lower-cost Dedicated burst pool; if none available, return graceful degradation response (trim output tokens) with structured status code.
   - Soft quality regression -> route a % of traffic to a higher-quality variant (possibly CPU-only rerank) and trigger alert to modelops; do not fail open to lower-quality variant automatically.
   - Regional outage -> prioritize tenants with higher-tier SLAs to alternate regions; follow data residency rules (skip cross-region) when privacy flag set.

   Notes: matrix rows are signals, columns are fallback actions. Each cell includes: preferred action, short justification, SLO impact estimate (latency/cost), and monitoring hooks.

3) Tradeoffs & rationale:
   - Deterministic vs heuristic: we prefer deterministic policy per signal for predictability, but allow a small heuristic layer (weighted sampling) for gradual rollouts and to detect regressions.
   - Cost vs reliability: cross-region fallback increases egress and cost; we conserve that for customers with reserved capacity or higher SLAs. Lower-tier customers get best-effort graceful degradation.
   - Observability: every fallback decision MUST emit a structured trace/span and a metric tag so Console can surface per-tenant fallback rates. This was non-negotiable (SLO for transparency).
   - Testing complexity: matrix expands test surface; prioritize automated chaos / fault-injection tests for hard failures and capacity rejections first.

4) Alternatives considered (shortlisted):
   - Global FIFO queueing: central buffer to smooth bursts — rejected due to single-point latency amplification and complexity across regions.
   - Opportunistic model ensemble fallback: run a cheap ensemble beside the main model for quality regressions — shelved for later due to cost and infra work.
   - Client-side retry + backoff enforcement: useful but insufficient for hard executor crashes and private deployments; keep as complementary approach.

5) Rollout and testing plan:
   - Phase 0 (lab): Implement matrix config schema + unit tests (owner: Dana) — 2 sprints
   - Phase 1 (staging canary): Add structured telemetry and implement two fallback cells (hard failure -> quantized variant, capacity rejection -> Dedicated burst) behind feature flag; run chaos tests (owner: Maya + SRE) — 1 sprint
   - Phase 2 (select tenants): Enable cross-region fallback for a small set of customers with agreed egress allowances (owner: Lina, sales notified) — 2–4 weeks observation
   - Phase 3 (gradual rollout): Incrementally enable additional cells and add quality regression policies with modelops gating.

6) Monitoring & Alerts:
   - New metrics: fallback.rate{signal,tenant,region}, fallback.latency.penalty, fallback.cost.delta.
   - Dashboards: per-tenant fallback heatmap, top failure signals week-over-week.
   - Alerts: spike in fallback.rate over X% for >15m -> P1 for SRE & on-call product engineer; isolated soft-quality fallbacks -> P2 to modelops.

7) API & config implications:
   - Routing policies must be expressible in current configuration language. We will add a small DSL for fallback priorities and constraints (e.g., allow_cross_region = true/false, prefer_quantized = true/false).
   - Default templates: low-tier, standard, enterprise — populated with sensible defaults and editable by tenant config.

Decisions made (consensus):
- Adopt the matrix approach as canonical source of truth for fallback behavior.
- Implement deterministic primary actions per signal with sampling knobs for monitoring and rollback.
- Cross-region fallback gated by tenant policy and billing consent.
- Instrumentation and traceability requirement mandatory before any public rollout.

Action items (owner — due):
- Draft initial matrix schema and examples (Dana) — due 2026-03-17
- Prototype telemetry tags and dashboard support (Maya + Samir) — due 2026-03-24
- Add unit tests & feature flag for two initial cells (Alex) — due 2026-03-24
- Coordinate with Product/Sales on tenant selection for Phase 2 (Lina) — due 2026-03-18
- Create chaos test scenarios for capacity rejection and executor crash (SRE: Samir) — due 2026-03-21

Open questions / risks:
- How to quantify SLO penalties for mixed fallbacks when routing sends partial traffic to lower-quality variants? (action: Priya will draft an SLO accounting proposal)
- Edge case: private on-prem deployments with strict egress rules — fallback options limited; need deterministic no-cross-region policy templates.
- Cost modeling: need finance sign-off on price adjustments or credits when fallbacks increase egress/cost.

Next steps: publish this note to the INF confluence draft, start schema PR draft, schedule a follow-up in 1 week for review of the schema prototype.

Permissions / doc etiquette: keep in shared drive; tag product & SRE for visibility; this is a working doc and will be updated as the schema and tests land.

Appendix: short example matrix cell (verbatim):
- signal: HARD_EXECUTOR_CRASH
  preferred_action: switch_to_quantized_variant_same_region
  secondary_action: mark_node_unhealthy_and_reprovision
  sample_rate_to_primary: 0.0 (immediate switch)
summary: Notes from an architecture scrub where the serving-runtime team aligned on a structured fallback matrix mapping failure signals to deterministic fallback actions, with telemetry, testing, and phased rollout plans.
